To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) operation scoring should be zero-cost, i.e., it should be possible to score operations without incurring a computational cost, and 2) operation selection should not be based on the magnitude but rather the sign of the operation's score.

(1) the magnitude of architectural weights is an unreliable proxy for operation selection and can lead to suboptimal architectures; (2) operation selection based on the gradient of architectural parameters is robust, efficient and can lead to superior architectures; (3) the gradient of architectural weights can be computed in a zero-cost manner using a single forward pass.

(1) operation scoring in differentiable NAS is a fundamental component of the algorithm, (2) operation scoring in existing differentiable NAS methods is flawed and leads to sub-optimal operation selection, (3) operation scoring can be improved via a novel zero-cost operation scoring method that does not require additional computational overhead, and (4) the proposed zero-cost operation scoring leads to significant improvement in performance of differentiable NAS methods.
